missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Топор' is masculine and stays in the nominative as the subject of 'лежит'. 'Острый' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'на земле' gives the location.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Топор' is an inanimate masculine noun, so its accusative equals the nominative as the object of 'возьми'. The imperative makes this a practical everyday command.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Топора' is the genitive after 'нет', expressing that something is lacking. 'Острого' is the agreeing masculine genitive adjective. A core negation pattern.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Топором' is the instrumental case naming the tool used to chop. 'Рубит' is the verb and 'дрова' the accusative object. Classic instrument usage.
Strategic focus: Dative recipient. 'Топору' is the dative form, here the thing given a rest. 'Старому' is the agreeing masculine dative adjective. A playful way to practise the dative ending.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'Топоре' is the prepositional form after 'на', showing where the nick is. 'Этом' agrees in the masculine prepositional. Useful for describing objects.

Strategic focus: Genitive singular after a numeral. After 'два' the noun takes the genitive singular 'топора'. 'В сарае' is the prepositional location. Counting two of something is a high-frequency pattern.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Топоры' is the nominative plural as the subject of 'висят'. 'Все' quantifies them, and 'на стене' gives the location. Good plural practice.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after a quantifier. After 'несколько' the noun takes the genitive plural 'топоров'. 'Новых' is the agreeing genitive plural adjective. A useful shopping construction.

Strategic focus: Nominative description. 'Топор' stays nominative as the subject. 'Этот' points at it and 'тяжёлый' is the agreeing masculine predicate adjective, reinforced by 'очень'. A clean descriptive card.
